label_reading_guide.title: Ingredient Order
label_reading_guide.content: Ingredients are listed by weight, from highest to lowest. The first ingredient makes up the most of the product.
label_reading_guide.tip: If sugar is in the first 3 ingredients, the product is likely high in sugar.

label_reading_guide.title: Understanding INS/E Numbers
label_reading_guide.content: INS (International Numbering System) and E numbers identify food additives. They're not necessarily harmful - they're just standardized codes.
label_reading_guide.tip: Look up unfamiliar numbers, but don't panic - many are natural substances like Vitamin C (INS 300).

label_reading_guide.title: May Contain Statements
label_reading_guide.content: These warnings indicate potential cross-contamination during manufacturing, not intentional ingredients.
label_reading_guide.tip: Important for allergies, but doesn't mean the ingredient is definitely present.

label_reading_guide.title: Hidden Sugars
label_reading_guide.content: Sugar appears under many names: dextrose, maltose, fructose, corn syrup, cane juice, and more.
label_reading_guide.tip: If multiple sugar types appear in one product, the total sugar content is higher than it seems.

label_reading_guide.title: Serving Size Tricks
label_reading_guide.content: Nutritional information is per serving, not per package. Check if one package contains multiple servings.
label_reading_guide.tip: A small candy bar might list '2 servings' to make calories appear lower.

label_reading_guide.title: Natural vs Artificial
label_reading_guide.content: 'Natural' doesn't always mean healthy. Natural flavors can be chemically complex and artificial ones can be simple.
label_reading_guide.tip: Focus on the overall ingredient list quality rather than just 'natural' labels.

myths_vs_facts.myth: All chemicals in food are harmful
myths_vs_facts.fact: Everything is made of chemicals, including water (H2O) and salt (NaCl). The dose makes the poison.
myths_vs_facts.explanation: Many safe substances become harmful only in extremely large quantities.

myths_vs_facts.myth: Natural is always better than artificial
myths_vs_facts.fact: Many artificial ingredients are identical to or safer than their natural counterparts.
myths_vs_facts.explanation: Artificial vanilla is chemically identical to natural vanilla but more consistent and affordable.

myths_vs_facts.fact: Organic foods can contain approved pesticides and additives, just different ones.
myths_vs_facts.explanation: Organic has specific standards but doesn't mean chemical-free.

myths_vs_facts.myth: If I can't pronounce it, it's bad
myths_vs_facts.fact: Complex names don't indicate danger. Vitamin B12 is cyanocobalamin.
myths_vs_facts.explanation: Scientific names sound scary but often describe harmless or beneficial substances.
